items.title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out
items.excerpt: NHS England has begun inviting women into EDITH, billed as the world's largest trial of AI in breast cancer screening (around 700,000 women), testing whether AI can replace one of the two human readers of mammograms and spot cancers earlier.
items.rationale: National-scale prospective trial (about 700,000 women) testing AI as a replacement second reader in NHS breast screening; a care-pathway change, not just a model paper.

items.title: AI in Mental Health Airlock to support safe innovation
items.excerpt: The MHRA is launching an 'AI in Mental Health Airlock', a new regulatory sandbox to test how safety of AI-enabled digital mental health technologies can be evaluated and regulated.
items.rationale: Primary regulator release: MHRA opens a sandbox specifically for AI mental-health tools, shaping how such devices will be evaluated and approved in the UK (assigned to medicine, not politics).

items.title: Photon pharmacy marketplace integrated with ChatGPT for clinicians
items.excerpt: Photon, a prescription infrastructure company, is now available as a plugin for ChatGPT to streamline prescribing for clinicians within a tool they already use. | The patient experience remains the same through Photon. What is new is where the clinician can write a prescription. Clinicians with a Ph
items.rationale: New release that puts e-prescribing inside ChatGPT for clinicians, moving a regulated clinical action into a general-purpose chatbot workflow.

items.title: 심부전 치료제 효과, AI로 환자별 예측한다
items.excerpt: 국내 연구진이 16가지 임상정보로 특정 심부전 치료제의 효과가 클 환자를 구분하는 AI 도구를 개발했다. 같은 약이라도 환자별로 달라지는 치료 혜택을 예측한다.
items.rationale: Korean team's AI tool uses 16 routine clinical variables to predict which heart-failure patients benefit most from a specific drug: treatment personalization at the prescribing decision.

items.title: Ambient AI documentation for structured EMR import in ophthalmology: consultation time, physician gaze behaviour and comparative accuracy
items.excerpt: EMR documentation contributes to physician workload and reduced patient–physician interaction, with ophthalmology particularly affected by specialist data requirements. This study compared ambient AI-assisted documentation for structured EMR import with conventional entry in standardised ophthalmic
items.rationale: Peer-reviewed clinic study measuring whether ambient AI that writes structured EMR fields changes consultation time, where the physician looks (patient vs screen) and record accuracy: direct evidence for clinicians weighing AI documentation in specialist clinics.
